text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Court rejects main points of legal bid by RWE to win compensation from regional government for nuclear power station built by the company but only briefly in use.
- Man confesses to murder of 10-year old girl.
- Opposition parties demand statement from Chancellor Helmut Kohl on unemployment.
- Helmut Werner, head of Daimler-Benz's carmaking arm Mercedes-Benz, loses power battle with Daimler chief Juergen Schrempp and decides to leave the company.
- Ruling coalition still undecided on whether pensions should be taxed more heavily.
HANDELSBLATT
- State of German government finances means Bonn in danger of missing Maastricht budget deficit target in 1997.
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer plans reform to make individual doctors more responsible for their drug orders.
- Planned tax reform will set basic income tax rate of 20 percent.
- Bundesbank calls for measures to make share ownership more attractive.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Regional state of Rhineland-Palatinate must fear multi-billion mark payout as result of RWE case against it.
- Commission clears parliamentary president Rita Suessmuth of allegations she used official aircraft for private trips.
- Bundesbank opposes general taxation on profits from share transactions.
- DAX share index closes just under 3,000-point level.
DIE WELT
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel certain to impose spending freeze on government departments in the next few weeks, coalition sources say.
- Departure of Werner means Mercedes-Benz will be absorbed into Daimler-Benz parent.
- Miners plan huge "human chain" to protest against government plans for mining industry.
